faults.fault: When widened 1.3x, the backbox art stretches rather than extending at the ends: the score displays double up ('00 00' becomes duplicated digit boxes), the speaker circles duplicate into overlapping pairs, and the side art is streaked. This reads as smeared texture, not a wider cabinet.

When widened and especially when made 1.4x taller, the stretched body/background texture shows obvious streaking, banding and seam lines down the sloped cabinet front and sides -- the extra height went into smeared texture instead of clean extension.

At 1.3x width the coin-door panel stays one size but its surrounding texture extrudes duplicate button slits and smeared speaker-hole shapes beside the door -- stretched decal rather than plain cabinet body on either side.

In the taller version, seam/streak bands run down the stretched playfield slope where the extra cabinet height was absorbed; the fixed rule is correct, but the panel texture behind it shows the smear rather than a plain deeper band of cabinet body.

wider_means: A wider pinball is simply a fatter single-player cabinet: the same playfield in a wider body, with the backbox housing, speaker panel and coin-door front panel all stretched to the new width and the legs set further apart.
taller_means: A taller pinball is the same machine standing on longer plain steel legs, with a deeper plain band of cabinet body under the playfield and the backbox lifted a little on a taller plain neck.
